items.title: Dick Katz interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 7, 2002
items.q: before Charlie Parker and Dizzy came up with those historic records

ctx.x: No. And he liked what he was doing, right?

He liked what he was doing. That’s another subject we won’t go into. But to give you a general answer I mean whether it was Fats Waller singing, I mean I think if he wanted to he, I mean he was a master pianist, I’m sure he enjoyed singing, but all that junk he had to sing, I mean there’s a lot of cynicism there. He’s making fun of all these songs. I think there’s no pat theories about it because — and I make statements like this and at the same time I’m talking like this I’m thinking of Dizzy Gillespie, the…
And the response from the audience was predictable, wasn’t it?
